title: Category map, drawn
subject: How to display a category map: what a set of blurred category words implies, and how the things they name fall

brief.result: Looking at one page, the reader can say what each word implies, whether the words are alternatives on one axis or values on different axes, where they overlap or leave gaps, which instances land outside their word, and which outcome holds.
musts: Each category word with the values it requires
The characteristics as axes with their values
Instances placed by their values, evidence one tap away

ideas.title: Periodic Table of Entries
ideas.encounter: A periodic table whose columns are the values of stands for and whose bands are the values of after written, each instance a tile in its cell, each word an outlined block over the cells it requires (registry (listed) a tinted group inside the registry (shape) block, stream a corner block, the private registry a detached row like the lanthanides), red tiles where usage drifts, occupied cells with no word and empty cells left standing as gaps, and the outcome as the table's footnote; tapping a tile opens its element card, all nine coded values with the evidence line behind each, and tapping a word's label lists the values it requires and the ones it leaves open.
ideas.helps: The reader judges alternatives against axes by position: registry (shape) and stream sit in opposite corners of one plane (rivals on the same two questions), registry (listed) is a tint on a third question rather than a rival cell, tending finding and session record sit in cells no word claims, and direct-to-main.csv and triggers.csv show red inside the block whose tint they lack.

ideas.title: Dichotomous Key
ideas.encounter: A field-guide key read top to bottom: each numbered couplet is one characteristic and its leads are that characteristic's values, a word stands where the key first reaches it (so the path above a word is what it requires and the dashed bracket below is what it leaves open), instances hang as chips where they key out, a chip that keys out away from the word it is called by is red, a lead that reaches no word says so, a characteristic that never splits anything is a struck couplet, and each word wears its outcome letter; tapping a chip replays that instance through the key with the evidence line that settled each couplet.
ideas.helps: A key asks only questions that separate, so the reader sees how many questions each word needs and of what kind: registry (shape) two (a region), registry (listed) one more and only a membership one (a list), the private registry out at the first (another kind of thing), stream and no word as rival leads of one couplet, and direct-to-main.csv and triggers.csv as misidentifications that key out under no.

ideas.title: Claimed Territory Map
ideas.encounter: A map whose land is the plane of stands for by after written: each word is a bordered territory on the cells it requires (registry (shape) and stream on opposite corners, registry (listed) a walled enclave inside the first), each instance a dot at its coordinates, unclaimed land hatched with its gaps and residents in view, web-tools-private an island off the coast; tapping a dot raises a sheet with that instance's nine values and the evidence line for each, and layer chips under the map recolor the dots by gets in, medium or lasts.
ideas.helps: It lets the reader judge at a glance that registry (shape) and stream are rivals splitting the same two axes while two corners lie unclaimed and two (tending finding, session record) have residents no word covers, that registry (listed) is a wall drawn on one more characteristic with direct-to-main.csv and triggers.csv standing outside it, and that the private registry is not on this land at all.

ideas.title: Zoned Street Plan
ideas.encounter: A street plan with one horizontal street per characteristic (nine, scrolling) and its values as blocks along it; each word paints the blocks it requires, each instance is a transit route that drops through every street and stops on its own value, a red stop marks a route leaving the zone of the word it is called by, and tapping any stop opens that instance's evidence for that value.
ideas.helps: Counting and comparing the streets a word paints tells a list from a region from a rival (registry (listed) adds one street of its own, registry (shape) paints two, stream paints other blocks of the same two, the private registry only the n/a lane), and a street where every route stops in one block, like keyed, plainly separates nothing.

ideas.title: One Axis at a Time
ideas.encounter: A vertical walk of numbered steps, one characteristic per step: each step splits the instances (dots) into that characteristic's values, colored word chips sit on the value each word requires (a dashed 'no word' chip marks a value nothing claims), a red dot is an instance outside its word and an amber dot a combination no word covers, steps not under study fold to a one-line result such as 'keyed: separates nothing', the last step states the verdict per word, and tapping any dot opens that instance's evidence for that step's value.
ideas.helps: It shows which characteristic actually separates the words, so the reader can judge whether they are rivals on one axis or answers to different questions, see the word that recurs across two steps as a region, and catch the step that splits nothing.

ideas.title: Words on Trial
ideas.encounter: A court docket with one case per word: the charge is the word's required values printed in fixed characteristic slots (dashed 'open' where it leaves one free), the exhibits called by that word line up beneath in the same slots with a check where they honor the charge and a red cell carrying the actual value where they break it, contested exhibits first, each case closes with a verdict stamp, an unclaimed panel holds instances whose combination no case covers, a ruling bar states the outcome, and tapping an exhibit row opens its evidence sheet, one quote per coded value.
ideas.helps: It lets the reader judge each word on its own terms, what it requires and whether usage honors it, while the aligned slots across cases show that the shape sense and stream fix the same two characteristics with opposite values and the listed sense adds a slot only it requires.

ideas.title: Cards in the Boxes
ideas.encounter: A grid whose columns are stands_for (a thing, an event) and whose rows are after_written (edited in place, never edited, edited until it ends), each word drawn as an outlined region over the boxes its required values pick out (registry (listed) as a dashed sub-box inside registry (shape), stream in the opposite corner), every instance a card in the box its own values put it in, a card whose called-by word disagrees with its box edged red, boxes no word outlines marked gap, web-tools-private held in an off-the-axes tray, and the outcome stated above; tapping a card opens a sheet with its nine coded values and the evidence for each, and tapping a region label lists the values that word requires.
ideas.helps: It helps the reader judge whether the words carve one space or several: registry (shape) and stream are opposite corners of the same two axes, registry (listed) is a boundary drawn by membership alone (writers.csv and direct-to-main.csv sit on either side of it with the same values), and tending finding and session record land in boxes no word claims.

ideas.title: Step Out of Line
ideas.encounter: One line per word, each backed by a wall of slots aligned under the shared axes (stands_for, after_written, listed, medium) showing the value the word requires or open, with the instances called by that word standing on the line, any instance whose value breaks the wall stepped forward below it with the broken value in red under its slot, a verdict tag at the head of each line, and a dashed bench for instances no line will take; tapping an instance opens its coded row with the evidence for each value, and tapping a red value opens the evidence for that one value.
ideas.helps: It helps the reader see what each word demands, which instances fail it, and read the outcome from why they fail: direct-to-main.csv steps out of registry (listed) on the listed slot alone, so that sense is a list; shape and stream fill the same two slots with opposite values, so they are regions on one pair of axes; and the private registry's wall reads n/a, so it is another kind of thing.
